findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key between related flusher timers
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the "spans.buffer.flusher.produce" timer and the "spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes" timing both use the tag key `{"shard": shard_tag}` (lines ~185-196), but the "spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce" timer uses `{"shards": shard_tag}` (plural) at line 199. This inconsistency means dashboards/alerts that filter or group by the `shard` tag will not pick up the `wait_produce` metric, breaking correlation between produce time and wait-for-produce time per shard group.

findings.title: New SpansBuffer instance created on every process restart without cleaning up the old one
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shards` (called both on initial startup and from `_ensure_processes_alive` on every restart, e.g. line 259) always constructs a brand-new `SpansBuffer(shards)` and overwrites `self.buffers[process_index]` (line 125). Previously, a single buffer object was created once in `__init__` and reused across restarts. Now, every unhealthy-process restart creates a fresh buffer/Redis client without explicitly closing the previous one, which can leak Redis connections over the lifetime of a long-running consumer that experiences repeated flusher process restarts.

findings.title: Memory backpressure check now aggregates memory info across per-process sub-buffers, risking double counting
findings.body: `submit()` now iterates `self.buffers.values()` (one `SpansBuffer` per flusher-process shard group, each created independently via `SpansBuffer(shards)`) and sums `get_memory_info()` results across them (lines 299-303), instead of calling `get_memory_info()` once on a single buffer covering all assigned shards as before. If `get_memory_info()` reports memory per underlying Redis host rather than per shard, and two different process groups contain shards that map to the same physical Redis host, that host's memory will be counted multiple times in the aggregated `used`/`available` sum. This directly feeds the `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage` hard-backpressure check used to avoid Redis OOM, so an incorrect aggregation could cause the check to behave incorrectly (false positive or negative backpressure).

findings.title: Dead/unused method `_create_process_for_shard`
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular, lines 127-132) is defined to look up the process group for a single shard and restart it, but it is never called anywhere in the class — `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards` (plural) directly with the already-known shard list. This leaves dead code in place, suggesting either an incomplete refactor or a helper that should have been used instead of duplicating the lookup logic.

findings.title: Added synchronization sleep is a no-op due to an earlier global monkeypatch
findings.body: In `test_basic`, `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` (line 15) patches the `time` module's `sleep` attribute globally for the whole test. The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` call at line 62, whose comment states it is meant to "give flusher threads time to process after drift change", therefore does nothing — it resolves to the same patched no-op function. The test's reliability for catching the flushed segment thus still depends entirely on uncontrolled thread scheduling rather than an actual wait, so the intended fix for test flakiness is ineffective and the test can still be flaky.

findings.title: New --flusher-processes option defaults to 1, disabling the new multi-process-per-shard behavior by default
findings.body: The new `--flusher-processes` CLI option defaults to `1`. Combined with `SpanFlusher.__init__`'s `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` logic, passing `1` (a truthy value) overrides the "one process per shard" default that would otherwise kick in when `max_processes` is `None`. As a result, the headline feature of this PR (spawning one flusher process per Redis shard) is not enabled unless operators explicitly override this CLI flag in deployment configuration — worth calling out since the PR description implies this is the new default behavior.

findings.title: Unrelated documentation change bundled into the multiprocessed-flusher PR
findings.body: The diff adds an unrelated "hasattr vs isinstance" anti-pattern snippet to CLAUDE.md (lines 449-458). This has no connection to the span-buffer flusher feature described in the PR and appears to be scope creep or an accidental inclusion, which makes the PR harder to review and could be better split into its own change.

findings.title: No test coverage for per-shard-group process restart/failure isolation
findings.body: The new tests only verify that shards are distributed across a limited number of processes (`test_flusher_processes_limit`); there is no test exercising `_ensure_processes_alive`/`_create_process_for_shards` restart path for the multi-process case — e.g. verifying that killing one shard-group's process only restarts that group's shards and leaves other groups' processes/buffers untouched, or that `process_restarts`/`process_healthy_since` are tracked independently per group. Given this PR substantially rewrote the restart logic to be per-process-group instead of global, this is an important gap in test coverage for a concurrency-sensitive code path.
